subject: Energy
title: Energy and Population Growth
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Energy and Population Growth.

hook.text: Fossil energy enabled explosive population growth—from 1 billion in 1800 to 8 billion today, fed by energy-rich farming.

buildup.text: The Haber-Bosch process (1913) turned natural gas into fertilizer—directly enabling food for billions more people.

discovery.text: Mechanized farming replaced human and animal labor—one modern farmer feeds 150 people versus 4 in pre-industrial times.

twist.text: Population growth is slowing—but energy demand keeps rising as billions aspire to middle-class living standards.

climax.text: Feeding and powering 10 billion by 2050 will require a massive energy expansion—mostly from clean sources.

punchline.text: Fossil energy fed billions—now clean energy must sustain them.

quiz.question: How many people can one modern farmer feed?
